newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - STEADY AWAITS FRESH INDICATORS.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS - STEADY AWAITS FRESH INDICATORS.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were steady at midday on Tuesday in the absence of fresh indicators, traders said.
"The market is not going anywhere right now. Many people are on the sidelines because the winter requirements are not clear," one trader said.
September gas oil was last quoted unchanged at $23.30/$23.50 per barrel with no deals seen, brokers said.

Traders said high stocks throughout the region for both gas oil and jet fuel is deterring players from picking up the forward swaps too much as the winter might turn out to be milder than expected as was the case last year.
Physical gas oil demand is thin as refiners in China, the region's largest importer, are operating at higher rates and are processing middle distillate rich crudes.
The double impact has cut back Chinese imports considerably and this has led to a build up of stocks in Singapore.
Even South Korea, China's natural supplier, has been forced to store gas oil in third party storage facilities such as in Subic Bay, in the Philippines, due to the poor demand from China.
India, the other big importer, has also cut back its purchases for September delivery down to a meagre 90,000 tonnes compared to 165,000 tonnes in August and 855,000 tonnes for July delivery.
Traders said unless the winter is very cold, demand will be easily met by the region's own capacity and the products that are currently in storage.
In the spot physical market on Monday, a U.S major sold to a Dutch trader 150,000-barrel for lifting Aug 27-31 at $22.50, up 10 cents from the previous trade on Friday.
Fuel oil trading was also quiet with prices range bound. September were last quoted unchanged at $102.00/$103.00, brokers said.
